check: whether step 4 could archive stale JUnit results, the same shape as the stale gametest report guarded at step 3
theRisk: Gradle marks the test task UP-TO-DATE when its inputs are unchanged, in which case it skips rather than re-running. build/test-results/test would then still hold the previous run's files, and step 4 would copy them as though they were this run's output.
itAppliesHere: No src/test or src/main commit has landed since 2026-10-08 06:00, and the files in that directory all carry a write time of 05:59:13 - the full-suite re-run from round 214. So the task may well be UP-TO-DATE when step 3 runs it alongside runGameTest.
andTheConsequenceIsBenignHere: Those 05:59 results are valid for the current source, because nothing under src/test or src/main has changed since. 103 XML files, 629 tests, zero failures. Archiving them would record the truth.
butItCannotBeAssumedInGeneral: The same skip after a source change would file stale results as current. The two cases look identical from the file listing alone - only the write time compared against the commit history distinguishes them.
soStep4NowRequires: Checking the files' write time and stating it, plus confirming with git log --since that src/test and src/main are unchanged since that time. A skipped task with unchanged sources gives valid results; a skipped task after changes does not.
whyThisCameUp: Step 3 guards against a stale gametest report by comparing a recorded SHA. Step 4 had no equivalent check, so this round asked the same question of it.
